blindSummary:
This state/province mirrors a neighbouring state/province's festival-entry religion screening: in a remote, largely tribal district, hardline religious-nationalist activists objected to sponsors and participants of minority faiths at a seasonal religious folk-dance festival, claiming damage to cultural purity, creating an ID-checked, religion-gated entry mechanism that outs gender-nonconforming visitors to informal enforcers. Unlike that neighbouring state/province, this one has no constituted transgender welfare board (absent from the list of 12 states and territories that have one). Additionally, in November 2024 a transgender woman was shot dead in an abandoned quarry in a contract killing reportedly arranged for a substantial sum in local currency, over rival claims to a community leadership seat - a single incident with no sourced second instance, recorded for pattern awareness rather than as a decisive factor.

Local risk sits modestly below the country-wide baseline. The combination of festival-entrance screening (visitor-facing, seasonal, an outing mechanism) and the absence of any state welfare apparatus distinguishes this state/province from the neighbouring one that carries the same screening but at least has a board. Compared with a border state/province whose harm is police-driven detention of suspected outsiders, the exposure here is community-organiser-driven at private-adjacent festivals, and the violence is a single unresolved incident. The gap to the national baseline is modest and confidence moderate.
